name: To Kill a Mockingbird
kicker: Harper Lee’s novel · Racial injustice seen through a child’s eyes
briefing: Through the eyes of young Scout Finch, this novel follows her father Atticus as he defends a Black man falsely accused of a crime he didn’t commit in 1930s Alabama. Scout and her brother Jem also spend the story chasing rumors about their mysterious, reclusive neighbor, Boo Radley. Harper Lee’s only novel for over fifty years, it won the Pulitzer Prize and remains one of the most-read books in American schools.

sample.note: the 12 real QBReader tossups for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked)

tossups.p: A reclusive neighbor in this novel is rumored to have once stabbed his own father with a pair of scissors. That neighbor, Arthur “Boo” Radley, leaves small gifts like soap figures and a pocket watch for two children in the knothole of a tree.
tossups.r: Those children’s father, a small-town lawyer, defends a Black man falsely accused of attacking a white woman named Mayella Ewell. For 10 points, name this novel about Scout and Jem Finch, written by Harper Lee.

tossups.p: A neighbor in this novel makes one character read aloud to her every afternoon as punishment for destroying her camellia bushes; that neighbor turns out to be a morphine addict named Mrs. Dubose. Later, the narrator calms an angry mob outside the jailhouse by asking Mr. Cunningham about his son.
tossups.r: The narrator’s father, attorney Atticus Finch, then defends Tom Robinson against a false charge brought by Mayella and Bob Ewell. For 10 points, name this novel narrated by young Scout Finch.

tossups.p: This novel’s narrator watches her father in court from the balcony reserved for Black spectators, alongside her brother and her friend Dill Harris. Her father once calmly shoots a rabid dog named Tim Johnson with a single blast, revealing why he had been nicknamed “One-Shot” as a boy.
tossups.r: That father, Atticus Finch, defends Tom Robinson at a racially charged trial in Maycomb, Alabama. For 10 points, name this novel by Harper Lee.

tossups.p: At the climax of this novel, a drunken man named Bob Ewell attacks two children walking home from a school pageant, where one of them had been dressed as a ham. A reclusive neighbor intervenes and carries an injured boy home to his father.
tossups.r: That neighbor, Arthur “Boo” Radley, is credited with saving Jem and Scout’s lives. For 10 points, name this novel by Harper Lee, set in the fictional town of Maycomb, Alabama.

tossups.p: A lawyer in this novel defends a disabled Black man whose left arm was crippled in a cotton-gin accident years earlier, a detail that undercuts the charge against him. Despite that evidence, an all-white jury convicts the defendant anyway.
tossups.r: That defendant, Tom Robinson, is later shot while trying to escape from prison. For 10 points, name this novel in which lawyer Atticus Finch takes on a doomed case in the Jim Crow South.

tossups.p: A family scorned by its neighbors as the poorest in town, headed by the violent, grudge-holding Bob Ewell, brings a false accusation against a hardworking Black field hand in this novel. That man’s employer, Link Deas, later threatens to invoke the “Ladies’ Law” to protect his widow.
tossups.r: The accused man, Tom Robinson, is defended at trial by Atticus Finch. For 10 points, name this novel narrated by Finch’s young daughter, Scout.

tossups.p: A man named Dolphus Raymond pretends to be a hopeless drunk, sipping Coca-Cola from a paper bag, so that his Maycomb neighbors will have an excuse for why he lives among Black families in this novel. Aunt Alexandra moves in with the narrator’s family partway through the story.
tossups.r: The narrator’s brother, Jem, is injured defending her from Bob Ewell near the novel’s end. For 10 points, name this novel about Scout and Jem Finch, written by Harper Lee.

tossups.p: This novel opens with its narrator recalling how her brother badly broke his arm when he was nearly thirteen, then flashes back to introduce Dill Harris, a visiting friend obsessed with the mysterious Radley house down the street. Its narrator and her brother find chewing gum, pennies, and carved soap figures hidden in a tree’s knothole.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this novel narrated by Jean Louise “Scout” Finch, in which her father Atticus defends Tom Robinson.

tossups.p: This novel’s title comes from a lesson its narrator’s father teaches about a harmless songbird that does nothing but sing — a creature it would be a sin to harm. A kindly neighbor, Miss Maudie Atkinson, loses her house to a fire one winter night.
tossups.r: That lesson comes to apply to both Tom Robinson and the reclusive Boo Radley. For 10 points, name this novel by Harper Lee, set in Depression-era Alabama.

tossups.p: Decades after this novel was published, an earlier draft of it reached shelves as the controversial “sequel” _Go Set a Watchman_, which depicts its narrator as an adult. In this novel, the narrator’s housekeeper, a Black woman named Calpurnia, helps raise her and her brother.
tossups.r: That narrator’s father, Atticus Finch, defends Tom Robinson, falsely accused of attacking Mayella Ewell. For 10 points, name this novel set in Maycomb, Alabama.

tossups.p: This novel’s narrator gets into a fistfight with her cousin Francis at Christmas after he insults her father’s choice of clients. That father calmly shoots a rabid dog, Tim Johnson, in the street, revealing a marksmanship skill his children never knew he had.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this novel in which attorney Atticus Finch defends Tom Robinson and raises his children, Jem and Scout, in Maycomb, Alabama.

tossups.p: This novel’s young narrator helps calm a mob gathered outside the county jail by chatting with Walter Cunningham about his son, not realizing the danger she has defused. Her father had been sitting outside that same jail to guard his client.
tossups.r: That client, Tom Robinson, still loses his case to an all-white jury despite clear proof of his innocence. For 10 points, name this novel by Harper Lee.

tossups.p: This novel’s narrator finds an unexpected blanket around her shoulders on a cold night while watching a neighbor’s house burn down, and only later do she and her brother realize their mysterious neighbor Boo Radley had put it there himself.
tossups.r: That same neighbor later saves the narrator and her brother from a nighttime attack by Bob Ewell. For 10 points, name this novel by Harper Lee, narrated by Scout Finch.

tossups.p: This novel’s central trial turns on evidence that its defendant’s left arm is essentially useless, making it unlikely he delivered the blows described by his accuser. That accuser’s father, Bob Ewell, spends the rest of the novel plotting revenge on the defense attorney’s family.
tossups.r: The defendant, Tom Robinson, is nonetheless convicted. For 10 points, name this novel in which Atticus Finch takes on Robinson’s doomed defense.

tossups.p: This novel follows two children, Jem and Scout Finch, growing up in the small Alabama town of Maycomb during the Great Depression. Their father, a widowed lawyer named Atticus Finch, agrees to defend a Black man falsely accused of a crime against a white woman.
tossups.r: Their mysterious neighbor, Boo Radley, eventually saves the children’s lives. For 10 points, name this novel by Harper Lee.

clues.t: Written by Harper Lee, published in 1960
Narrated by young Scout Finch (Jean Louise Finch)
Scout’s father, lawyer Atticus Finch, is the moral center of the novel
Set in the fictional town of Maycomb, Alabama, during the Great Depression
Atticus defends Tom Robinson, a Black man falsely accused of attacking Mayella Ewell
Despite clear evidence of his innocence, an all-white jury convicts Tom Robinson anyway
Scout and Jem’s summer friend Dill Harris visits from out of town each year
Scout defuses a lynch mob outside the jail by talking to Mr. Cunningham about his son
The reclusive neighbor Boo Radley leaves small gifts for the children in a tree’s knothole
Bob Ewell attacks Jem and Scout after a Halloween pageant where Scout is dressed as a ham
Boo Radley saves the children and carries Jem home; Bob Ewell is found dead nearby
Title theme: it is a sin to harm an innocent songbird that only sings for people to enjoy
Nicknamed “One-Shot,” Atticus kills a rabid dog named Tim Johnson with a single shot
At trial, Atticus shows that Tom Robinson’s left arm is crippled, undercutting Mayella’s account
After his conviction, Tom Robinson is shot and killed while trying to escape from prison
Jem is forced to read aloud to the morphine-addicted Mrs. Dubose after destroying her camellia bushes
Calpurnia, the Finches’ Black housekeeper, helps raise Scout and Jem
Aunt Alexandra moves in with the Finch family partway through the novel
Dolphus Raymond fakes being a drunk, sipping Coca-Cola from a paper bag, to excuse living among Black neighbors
Tom Robinson’s employer, Link Deas, later threatens to invoke the “Ladies’ Law” to protect his widow
An earlier draft was published in 2015 as the controversial novel _Go Set a Watchman_
Rumored to have once stabbed his father with a pair of scissors, Boo Radley has not been seen in public for years
Kind neighbor Miss Maudie Atkinson’s house burns down one winter night
The Ewells, including Bob and his daughter Mayella, are the poorest, most looked-down-on family in Maycomb

trap.title: This novel, or its “sequel”?
trap.body: An early draft of this novel was published in 2015 as _Go Set a Watchman_, featuring an adult Jean Louise “Scout” Finch returning home from New York and a very different, more old-fashioned Atticus. The two books share characters and a setting but very different plots and reputations.
trap.fix: A child narrator, the Tom Robinson trial, or Boo Radley means _To Kill a Mockingbird_. A grown-up Scout visiting Maycomb from New York means _Go Set a Watchman_.
trap.line: Real answer line: To Kill a Mockingbird
